title: Multi-modal virtual environments for education with haptic and olfactory feedback
central_proposition: Immersive, multi-modal virtual reality (VR) technology, integrating haptic and olfactory feedback, provides an alternative and effective educational process for abstract scientific concepts by supporting constructivist learning principles like interaction, size, transduction, and reification.

concept_definitions.name: Virtual Reality (VR)
concept_definitions.definition: Computer-generated, interactive, and three-dimensional environments into which users are immersed, or which add graphical information to the perceived natural environment that is updated according to the movements and position of the user.

concept_definitions.name: Haptics
concept_definitions.definition: Refers to physical interactions with virtual environments (VEs).

concept_definitions.name: Constructivism
concept_definitions.definition: An educational perspective where knowledge is acquired through self-directed activity, motivation, and naturalistic learning.

concept_definitions.name: Immersion
concept_definitions.definition: The feeling of presence in the virtual environment, enhanced by integrating multiple senses into a single display system.

concept_definitions.name: Interaction
concept_definitions.definition: Manipulating virtual objects using controls similar to those of real objects, taking different viewpoints at will and hence operating with intuitive immediacy.

concept_definitions.name: Size
concept_definitions.definition: The ability to change VEs' physical size, allowing the user to navigate and interact in macro-, micro- and even nano-worlds.

concept_definitions.name: Transduction
concept_definitions.definition: The perception of non-perceptible signals such as ultrasound or infrared light.

concept_definitions.name: Reification
concept_definitions.definition: The transformation of abstract ideas into perceptible representations.

concept_definitions.name: Autonomy
concept_definitions.definition: The independence of the VE from the user's actions, where the laws of physics apply in space and time inside the VE.

argument_structure: The paper reviews existing VR applications with haptic and olfactory feedback, highlighting their educational potential. It then describes the authors' multi-modal human-scale VR system (VIREPSE) and an application ('Haptic Atomic') for teaching the Bohr atomic model. Finally, it proposes different configurations for this application, linking them to constructivist learning principles and discussing the significance of multi-modal feedback for knowledge-building and retention.
mechanism_or_causal_logic: Multi-modal (visual, haptic, auditory, olfactory) and immersive VR environments enhance learning by increasing immersion and presence, which improves cognitive and sensory-motor performance. This approach supports constructivist learning by allowing students to actively build knowledge through direct experience and manipulation of abstract concepts. Specifically, reification (transforming abstract ideas into perceptible representations) is facilitated by haptic force feedback and specific scents, making concepts more tangible and understandable. Olfactory cues, with their strong emotional and memory links, enhance retention and recall of learned materials. Haptic feedback provides direct physical cues, compensating for limitations of pure visual representation and making interactions more intuitive.

findings.consequent: Knowledge-building experiences and alternative educational process
findings.mechanism: VR incorporates characteristics like immersion, presence, direct engagement, autonomy, and interactivity, which support constructivist learning.
findings.quote: It has been suggested that immersive virtual reality (VR) technology allows knowledge-building experiences and in this way provides an alternative educational process.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Youngblut 1998, Dede et al. 1997, Roussos and Gillingham 1998, Mikropoulos et al. 1998, Winn and Windschitl 2001

findings.consequent: Suitability for sciences requiring higher visualization and interaction
findings.mechanism: VR allows visualization of complex data and building of more adequate conceptual models.
findings.quote: VR technology suits very well the needs of sciences that require a higher level of visualization and interaction...
findings.empirical_support_cited: Bryson 1996, Dede et al. 1999, Salzman et al. 1999

findings.antecedent: Integration of many senses into a single display system (multi-modal feedback)
findings.consequent: Feeling of presence; Cognitive and sensory-motor performance
findings.mechanism: Multi-modal input provides richer, more congruent information, enhancing the user's sense of being 'there' and facilitating more effective interaction.
findings.quote: Indeed, integrating many senses into a single display system increases the feeling of presence in the environment and both cognitive and sensory-motor performance.

findings.consequent: Sense of presence; Emotion; Salient spatial cues
findings.mechanism: Olfaction is an 'associative' and 'emotional' sense, capable of shifting attention, adding novelty, and enhancing mental state, contributing to a richer environmental experience.
findings.quote: Previous studies have reported that compelling olfactory cues have the potential to enhance the sense of presence (Barfield and Danas 1996; Dinh et al. 1999), invoke emotion, and provide salient spatial cues (Von Békésy 1964).
findings.empirical_support_cited: Barfield and Danas 1996, Dinh et al. 1999, Von Békésy 1964

findings.consequent: Memory retention and recall (especially for emotionally charged content)
findings.mechanism: Olfactory memory has 'Proustian characteristics' including resistance to interference, uniqueness, and independence from other modalities, making smell-related memories more enduring and emotionally potent.
findings.quote: Olfactory memory is considered to have reliable qualities, commonly known as “Proustian characteristics” which include resistance to interference, uniqueness, and independence from other modalities (Herz and Engen 1996; Annett 1996; Danthiir et al. 2001).
findings.empirical_support_cited: Herz and Eich 1995, Herz 1998, Herz and Engen 1996, Annett 1996, Danthiir et al. 2001

findings.mechanism: Direct neural link between olfactory processing and cerebellar function.
findings.quote: Additionally, odors have been found to activate the cerebellum, which is involved in motor learning.

findings.consequent: Human performance (speed and precision) in interactive tasks
findings.mechanism: Haptic feedback provides direct physical cues that complement visual information, reducing misjudgment of virtual object properties and making interactions more intuitive.
findings.quote: Several experimental studies established that haptic sensations provide essential information during interactive tasks. Indeed, they have demonstrated a dramatically improved human performance in terms of speed and precision when supported by force and touch feedback...
findings.empirical_support_cited: Ouh-Young et al. 1989, Richard and Coiffet 1995, Birmanns and Wriggers 2003, Wu et al. 1999

findings.consequent: Acquisition and retention of abstract concepts
findings.mechanism: Direct physical interaction with abstract concepts (e.g., electron jumping orbits) requires physical energy expenditure, creating a more tangible and memorable experience, aligning with constructivist principles.
findings.source: Section 6, Discussion; Section 7, Conclusion and future work
findings.quote: Moreover, we propose that human-scale haptic interaction (SPIDAR-H) leads to better acquisition and retention thanks to bigger physical and psychic/emotional implications of the user.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Cai et al. 1997, Dede et al. 1997, Youngblut 1998, Roussos and Gillingham 1998

findings.antecedent: Reification (transformation of abstract ideas into perceptible representations) via multi-modal feedback (haptic, olfactory)
findings.consequent: Understanding of abstract concepts; Knowledge construction
findings.mechanism: Making abstract concepts tangible (haptic force for energy levels) and associating them with distinct sensory cues (scents for quantum numbers) provides concrete representations that facilitate conceptualization and learning.
findings.source: Section 6, Discussion; Section 7, Conclusion and future work
findings.quote: Reification, in this case, refers to the abstract concept of the Bohr atom model and might lead students to understand that the electron is restricted to a discrete orbital level and that some external quantized quantity of energy is required to make it jump from the first energy level to a higher one.

findings.antecedent: Association of specific scents with energy levels or quantum numbers
findings.consequent: Reification reinforcement; Conceptualization of energy level degeneracy and orbital shape
findings.mechanism: Olfactory cues, with their strong memory links, provide unique, memorable markers for abstract states, aiding in their differentiation and understanding.
findings.quote: Furthermore, we put forward the assumption of reification reinforcement through the association of a specific scent with each energy level linked to haptic feedback.

testable_hypotheses_or_predictions: Different configurations that support interaction, size and reification through the use of immersive and multi-modal (visual, haptic, auditory and olfactory) feedback are proposed for further evaluation.
The present work tackles the haptical perception of the quantization of the orbitals' state energy levels by means of different haptic feedback devices.
Within the framework of our 'Haptic Atomic' application, we describe different VE configurations that we will investigate and compare by analyzing undergraduate student's performance.
The experiments carried out will allow us to test these hypotheses [regarding reification reinforcement through scent association].
We propose that human-scale haptic interaction (SPIDAR-H) leads to better acquisition and retention thanks to bigger physical and psychic/emotional implications of the user.

The following step will be to verify the effectiveness of the simulation in comparison to traditional teaching methods and we may be able to understand the educational benefits of applying haptics to a human-scale way of learning.
bridge_warrants: The paper explicitly links VR features (immersion, presence, direct engagement, autonomy, interactivity) to constructivist learning theory, arguing that these features support active knowledge construction.
It connects multi-modal feedback to the concept of 'presence' in VR, proposing that enhanced presence, in turn, improves cognitive and sensory-motor performance.
The framework leverages the unique properties of olfactory memory, specifically its 'Proustian characteristics' and strong emotional links, to enhance retention and recall of learned materials.
methodological_critiques: Evaluations of virtual learning environments have been limited by the size and focus of research projects and the maturity of VEs, often being informal and employing only one iteration.
Early studies primarily focused on usability questions like 'Can the VE be used by students?' and 'Which input devices are preferable?'.
It is impossible to directly compare VR-based learning with traditional teaching methods because different things are learned, making direct comparative studies challenging.
model_structure: The paper proposes a conceptual framework for designing educational VR environments. This framework integrates multi-modal feedback (visual, haptic, auditory, olfactory) and human-scale immersion, guided by constructivist learning principles. Its goal is to facilitate the understanding and retention of abstract scientific concepts through 'reification' – the transformation of abstract ideas into perceptible, interactive representations. The VIREPSE platform and 'Haptic Atomic' application serve as a concrete instantiation of this framework, with various configurations proposed for empirical testing of its propositions.
limitations: Integration of the sense of smell in VEs has primarily been a research issue, with few practical applications.
String-based haptic interfaces are complex to set up and control.
A major problem with emitting scents is their wide diffusion and slow dissipation.
Hypersensitivity to scents is a concern that requires careful attention.
A thorough understanding of odor quality determinants and the effects of odorant delivery parameters (concentration, duration, frequency, flow rate) is needed for perceptually accurate stimuli.
Evaluations of virtual learning environments have been limited by project scope, VE maturity, and often informal, single-iteration studies.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: The integration of haptic, olfactory, visual, and auditory feedback in virtual environments enhances the richness and realism of the experience, leading to more effective information processing.
Multi-modal virtual environments facilitate active, hands-on learning experiences that align with the principles of experiential learning, promoting deeper understanding and knowledge construction.

By distributing information across multiple sensory channels, multi-modal virtual environments can optimize cognitive load, potentially reducing overload on a single modality and enhancing learning efficiency.
